$comment:
Conformance runner registry, v0 — the non-vacuity guard for the conformance suite itself.

WHY THIS FILE EXISTS.
A shared corpus only produces cross-language identity if BOTH implementations
feed it to the code that actually ships. A runner that re-derives the behaviour
inline and checks its own reconstruction is tautological: it proves the
primitive it reimplemented is deterministic, stays green while the shipped code
drifts underneath it, and reads as coverage in every report.

That is not hypothetical. The Node byte anchor for the canonical idempotency
digest did exactly this -- it rebuilt the canonical form with JSON.stringify,
hashed its own reconstruction with createHash, and never once called the shipped
payloadHash. It had been green the whole time while proving nothing.

Stating the rule in a comment does not prevent the next corpus from repeating
it. This registry makes the rule machine-checked:

  python/tests/test_conformance_runner_hygiene.py
  node/tests/conformanceRunnerHygiene.test.ts

WHAT IS ENFORCED.
  1. COVERAGE. Every corpus in conformance/ has a runner entry for both
     languages. Adding a corpus without runners fails CI, so a corpus can never
     sit unexercised while appearing to be part of the suite.
  2. REACHES THE SHIPPED CODE. Each runner imports the symbol named in
     `must_import` from the SDK source. A runner that stopped calling shipped
     code would have to drop that import to do so.
  3. CANNOT RE-DERIVE. No runner imports a primitive from `forbidden_imports`.
     Without crypto and hashing primitives a runner has no way to rebuild the
     behaviour it is meant to verify, so the tautology is unreachable rather
     than merely discouraged.
  4. NON-VACUOUS. The guard asserts its own scan found files. A guard that
     silently matched nothing would be the same disease one level further up.

This file is the registry of what must be exercised. invariants.v0.json is the
registry of what must hold. Neither is optional, and neither is self-verifying
without the other.

corpora.exercises: the shipped public wrap() LITE filter
the shipped canonical idempotency payload hash
recorded decisions replayed against the shipped wrap() and doctor.check
the shipped AI-native decision reader (parse_authority_decision / parseAuthorityDecision)

the shipped Core-attestation verifier: the canonical-message rebuild, the signature and signing-key pins, host / nonce / freshness, the silence checks (a ledger head that did not advance, and a report that never arrived), and the expected-inventory comparison Core explicitly does not make

the shipped Ed25519 verification the attestation signature check rests on. The two SDKs reach it differently — OpenSSL via node:crypto on one side, RFC 8032 in Python int arithmetic on the other, because the LITE install is dependency-free by contract — so what they must agree on is written down rather than assumed

forbidden_dynamic_import.$comment: Banning static crypto imports alone is walked straight past by dynamic import. Flagged independently by cursor and agy in the 2026-07-19 cross-review.

not_corpora_reasons.$comment: Every exemption must state why. An undocumented exemption list is where a conformance suite quietly stops meaning anything, so the guard rejects entries with no reason.
not_corpora_reasons.invariants.v0.json: The declaration of what must hold, not a vector corpus. It has no input/expected pairs to run; it is instead validated directly by the hygiene guards (customer_facing derivation, evidence paths, enforcement vocabulary).
not_corpora_reasons.runners.v0.json: This registry itself. Exercised by the hygiene guards that read it; it contains no vectors of its own.
not_corpora_reasons.backends.v0.json: The registry of WHAT the invariants must hold for (surfaces, backends, and the backend x invariant coverage product). Like invariants.v0.json it contains no input/expected vectors to run; it is validated directly by test_backend_registry.py / backendRegistry.test.ts, which parse the SDK source and refuse any export that is neither a registered backend nor a justified exclusion.
not_corpora_reasons.irreversible_ops.v0.json: The irreversibility classification of the SDK's shipped operation surface (INV-7, SDK form). Contains no input/expected vectors: it is validated directly by test_irreversible_ops.py and irreversibleOps.test.ts, which parse the shipped generated client and refuse any operation that is unclassified, any docstring-declared irreversibility classified otherwise, and any growth of the ungated single-call set.
